relations.myth: Kherty ferries the king identified as Sokar
relations.note: Kherty supplies transport for the dead king after he assumes Sokar's identity.

relations.myth: Khnum makes Kherty's ferry in Sokar's scene
relations.note: Khnum constructs the sacred ferry used to transport the king identified as Sokar.

relations.myth: Horus raises and carries the king as Sokar
relations.note: Horus lifts and bears the dead king in Sokar's name and henu barque.

relations.myth: Horus transmits the restored Eye in Rosetau
relations.note: Horus offers or transmits the restored Eye in Sokar's desert realm; the recipient's identity is disputed.

relations.myth: Thoth ferries the deceased as Sokar
relations.note: Thoth is asked to ferry the deceased as Sokar presiding over a divine bark.
Ptah and Sokar fuse, combining Memphite creation and craftsmanship with necropolis power.
Sokar fuses with Osiris, joining hidden death and Memphite necropolis power to resurrection.
Sokar joins Ptah and Osiris in a tripartite funerary manifestation.
Sokar joins Osiris and Ptah in a tripartite funerary manifestation.

relations.myth: Re traverses Sokar's sandy underworld realm
relations.note: Re's nocturnal passage animates Sokar's hidden corpse-region and enables renewal.

relations.myth: Aker guards Sokar's cavern beneath the mound
relations.note: Aker encloses and guards the subterranean cavern occupied by Sokar.

relations.myth: Sokar's cavern mediates Re and Osiris
relations.note: Sokar's hidden realm mediates the conjunction of Osirian death with solar renewal.
Hathor manifests locally, protects the rite, and accompanies Sokar's ceremonial entrance.

relations.myth: Paired chapels and festival equipment at Abydos
relations.note: Sokar and Nefertem share chapels and associated festival equipment in Seti I's temple.
Isis appears beside Ptah-Sokar-Osiris and protects or revives its Osirian component.
Nut appears on composite funerary figures and extends protection over the deceased god.
Anubis co-occurs with the composite god as embalmer and guardian.
The collective flanks the composite god and protects the organs and deceased.
